newsitem.title: USA: Hayes agrees to buy Cardinal Technologies.
newsitem.headline: Hayes agrees to buy Cardinal Technologies.

text.p: Hayes Microcomputer Products Inc on Thursday said it signed a letter of intent to acquire Cardinal Technologies Inc for an undisclosed amount.
Hayes, a modem maker, said it signed the letter with Vulcan Ventures Inc, which owns 75 percent of Cardinal.
Based in Lancaster, Pennsylvania, Cardinal makes modems and ISDN adapters. Vulcan is led by Paul Allen, a co-founder of computer software giant, Microsoft Corp.
Jim Jonez, director of product marketing at Cardinal, told Reuters the outlines of the deal earlier Thursday.
Hayes expects to complete the deal by the end of March.
It said it planned to close Cardinal's Lancaster factory and consolidate operations at its Norcross, Georgia, facility. The company did not say how many jobs would be affected by the move.
"Hayes plans to fully support and market the Cardinal brand through Hayes' Practical Peripherals business unit, focused on consumer and SOHO (small office/home office) markets," it said.
In a separate transaction, Vulcan said it would become an investor in Hayes. "Hayes plans to explore other business opportunities with companies within the Paul Allen Group of companies," it added.
Hayes, which dominated the modem industry in its first decade, lost ground to low-cost clone makers in the late 1980s. It underwent a Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 1994.
The company ranks as the second-largest consumer modem maker after U.S. Robotics Corp Hayes sells software and a range of Wide Area Networking (WAN) equipment.
Founder Dennis Hayes reportedly owns a majority of his company's stock.
